title: Authority map and anti-bypass boundaries
summary: CMS owns approved content and brand intention; institutional policy owns review/operative rules; social library owns semantic exposure and local publication sequencing; adapter owns provider protocol proof only; brand analytics own effects.
invariants: A social surface or discovered capability is descriptive, not a publication grant.
Authorisation and scoped capability must independently pass, then SocialLibrary policy must permit dispatch.

The public lower-level SocialLibrary~execute and SocialPublicationService are currently callable outside the strict scoped facade; production exposure MUST enforce only SocialScopedPublicationService, and redesign to make bypass structurally impossible is a documented gap.
A provider transport receipt is not delivery proof, a conversation graph entry is not a verified inbound event, and a brand-effect claim is not causal proof.
Spend, marketplace commerce, private-message outreach and moderation must have separate effectful authorisation.
procedure: Expose only the strict facade at application/service registration.
Resolve exact provider/account/surface/action live capability and production publication approval.
Use existing institutional policy, identity, API Client and Secret Broker; never implement lookalike mechanisms.

provenance.claim: Strict facade does not conceal lower-level public classes
Adapter is a provider wrapper, not an authorizer

integrates_with: API Client / Secret Broker / Identity (external authorities)
